CHALLENGE C0003 | If `total_net == 0` and `tests_passed is True`, returning `SAFE` is correct. A fix that repairs a logic bug (verified by passing tests) without introducing new linting issues is a safe, successful fix. Forcing it to `NEUTRAL` would wrongly prevent valid logic fixes from being applied.

CHALLENGE C0039 | The proposed regex fix `(?:\s+\[([^\]]+)\])?$` still fails because the preceding `(.*?)` is lazy and will expand to consume the `[code]` to satisfy the `$` anchor. Additionally, the entire fix is moot because `run_mypy` does not pass `--show-error-codes` to the binary, meaning mypy will never output the codes in the first place.

CHALLENGE C0046 | `os.path.commonpath` only raises `ValueError` on Windows when paths are on different drives. The system context explicitly defines the hardware target as "M1 8GB Mac". On macOS, all absolute paths share the `/` root, so `commonpath` will never fail. This constraint is moot for the PoC.

DESCRIPTION: FIND — In `_apply_fix_to_source` Strategy 3, the `line_pattern` regex `r"... \s*->\s*(.+)"` lacks `re.DOTALL`. Because `.` does not match newlines, `(.+)` only captures up to the end of the first line. If a proposed fix contains a multi-line replacement block, all lines after the first are silently dropped, corrupting the code.
FOLLOW: The sandbox will apply and test a truncated, broken fix. This guarantees a `SyntaxError` or logic failure, causing `evaluate_fix` to falsely reject valid multi-line fixes as HARMFUL.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Add `re.DOTALL` and make the target group lazy but bounded by the next `Line` marker or end-of-string.
